chapter_title_en: Story of Avtandil's Return to Arabia
chapter_expert_explanation_en: Avtandil rides back to Arabia, is joyfully welcomed by Shermadin and King Rostevan, and recounts Tariel's full story to Queen Tinatin, who praises his fidelity and urges him to fulfill his oath to return and aid his sworn brother.

stanzas.english_translation: When he was gone thence sadness was surely slaying him; he scratched his face, he rent the rose (of his cheeks), his hand he shortened; all the beasts licked up the blood that flowed from him. His swift pace shortened the long course.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 30 ('Story of Avtandil's Return to Arabia', Stanza 672; Wardrop Stanza 654): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Arabia, is joyfully welcomed by Shermadin and King Rostevan, and recounts Tariel's full story to Queen Tinatin, who praises his fidelity and urges him to fulfill his oath to return and aid his sworn brother.

მუნ მოვიდა, სადა იგი მისნი სპანი დაეყარნეს
ნახე, იცნეს, რაგვარადცა ჰმართებს, აგრე გაეხარნეს.
შერმანდისცა ახარებდეს, ფიცხლად, თავნი მისკენ არნეს:
და “მოვიდაო, აქანამდის ვითვის ლხინი გაგვემწარნეს!”
stanzas.english_translation: He came there where he had parted from his armies. They saw him, they knew him, they rejoiced in such manner as was fitting. They told the good tidings to Shermadin too; .men quickly ran to him: "He is come for whose sake hitherto joy has been embittered to us."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 30 ('Story of Avtandil's Return to Arabia', Stanza 673; Wardrop Stanza 655): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Arabia, is joyfully welcomed by Shermadin and King Rostevan, and recounts Tariel's full story to Queen Tinatin, who praises his fidelity and urges him to fulfill his oath to return and aid his sworn brother.

აკოცებდა, სიხარულით ცრემლსა ღვრიდა ველთა მრწყველსა;
ესე თქვა თუ: “ნეტარ, ღმერთო, ცხადსა ვხედავ, ანუ ბნელსა?
და მე ვით ღირს ვარ ამას, რომე თვალნი ჩემნი ჭვრეტდენ მრთელსა!”
stanzas.english_translation: He went to meet him, he embraced him, he put his mouth on his (Avt’handil's) hand, pouring forth tears he joyfully kissed the destroyer in the field. Thus he spoke: "O God, do I see really or darkly? How am I worthy of this, that mine eyes should gaze upon thee (safe and) sound!"

stanzas.english_translation: The knight saluted him low, he put face upon face; he said: "I thank God that no grief afflicts thee!" The magnates did homage, whoever was worthy kissed him; there was great jubilation, great and small alike rejoiced.

მოვიდა ნახვად ყოველი მის ქალაქისა კრებული.

stanzas.english_translation: They came where a dwelling-house had been built; all the city was assembled to see him; forthwith he sat down to feast, gay, proud, merry; an assemblage of tongues could not fully describe the joy of that day.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 30 ('Story of Avtandil's Return to Arabia', Stanza 676; Wardrop Stanza 658): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Arabia, is joyfully welcomed by Shermadin and King Rostevan, and recounts Tariel's full story to Queen Tinatin, who praises his fidelity and urges him to fulfill his oath to return and aid his sworn brother.

ანუ ვით პოვა იგი ყმა, მისგანვე მზედ დასახული

და “უმისოდ მყოფსა სწორად მიჩნს ჩემთვის დარბაზი და ხული”
stanzas.english_translation: He told Shermadin, he narrated to him all he had seen--how he had found that knight whom he likened to the sun. Avt’handil was hampered by tears; he said with half-closed eyes: "Without him it seems to me alike to dwell in palace or hut."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 30 ('Story of Avtandil's Return to Arabia', Stanza 677; Wardrop Stanza 659): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Arabia, is joyfully welcomed by Shermadin and King Rostevan, and recounts Tariel's full story to Queen Tinatin, who praises his fidelity and urges him to fulfill his oath to return and aid his sworn brother.

“შენი წასვლა არვინ იცის, რაცა მითხარ, აგრე ვქმენა!”
მას დღე მუნით არ წავიდა, ინადიმა, განისვენა,

stanzas.english_translation: (Shermadin) told him all the home news: "None knows of thy departure; whatever thou toldst me so have I done." He went not thence that day, he feasted and rested; at dawn he mounted, he set out when the sun enlightened the day.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 30 ('Story of Avtandil's Return to Arabia', Stanza 678; Wardrop Stanza 660): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Arabia, is joyfully welcomed by Shermadin and King Rostevan, and recounts Tariel's full story to Queen Tinatin, who praises his fidelity and urges him to fulfill his oath to return and aid his sworn brother.

შერმადინ მახარობელი წავა მისლვისა მათისა,

stanzas.english_translation: He sat no more at feasting, nor stayed he again private; Shermadin, the bearer of good tidings, went to announce (Avt’handil's) arrival; swiftly he fared, in three days he made a ten days’ journey. That lion (Avt’handil) rejoiced that he was to see the sun's rival.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 30 ('Story of Avtandil's Return to Arabia', Stanza 679; Wardrop Stanza 661): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Arabia, is joyfully welcomed by Shermadin and King Rostevan, and recounts Tariel's full story to Queen Tinatin, who praises his fidelity and urges him to fulfill his oath to return and aid his sworn brother.

შესთავლა: “მეფე უკადრი ხარმცა მორჭმით და დიდობით!
ამა საქმესა ვიკადრებ შიშით, კრძალვით და რიდობით,

stanzas.english_translation: He sent a message: "O king, proud art thou in might and majesty! I venture to tell thee this thing with fear, respect and precaution: I esteemed myself worthless in that I had learned nought of that knight; now I know and will tell thee all; I come in joy and safety."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 30 ('Story of Avtandil's Return to Arabia', Stanza 680; Wardrop Stanza 662): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Arabia, is joyfully welcomed by Shermadin and King Rostevan, and recounts Tariel's full story to Queen Tinatin, who praises his fidelity and urges him to fulfill his oath to return and aid his sworn brother.

როსტევან, მეფე უკადრი, მორჭმული, შეუპოველი, -
შერმადინ მოციქულობა თვით მოახსენა ყოველი:

stanzas.english_translation: Rostevan is a king, proud, puissant, imperious, (so) Shermadin delivered all his message in person: "Avt’handil comes to the royal presence having found that knight." The king said: "(Now) I know that which I entreated and prayed for from God."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 30 ('Story of Avtandil's Return to Arabia', Stanza 681; Wardrop Stanza 663): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Arabia, is joyfully welcomed by Shermadin and King Rostevan, and recounts Tariel's full story to Queen Tinatin, who praises his fidelity and urges him to fulfill his oath to return and aid his sworn brother.

stanzas.english_translation: Shermadin made report to T’hinat’hin, that night-less light: "Avt’handil comes to thy presence; he brings thee pleasing news." Thereat, light flashed forth from her, even braver than the sun's. She gave him a gift, and robes to all his people.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 30 ('Story of Avtandil's Return to Arabia', Stanza 682; Wardrop Stanza 664): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Arabia, is joyfully welcomed by Shermadin and King Rostevan, and recounts Tariel's full story to Queen Tinatin, who praises his fidelity and urges him to fulfill his oath to return and aid his sworn brother.

stanzas.english_translation: The king mounted and went to meet the knight who was coming thither, for this (honour) the sun-faced one incurred a great debt (of gratitude); joyous and warm-hearted they met, and some of the multitude of magnates seemed as if drunken.

stanzas.english_translation: When he approached, the knight alighted and did homage to the king. Rosten, possessed by excess of joy, kissed him. Glad-hearted and merry they entered the royal hall; all there assembled rejoice at the arrival of the knight.

stanzas.english_translation: Avt’handil, the lion of lions, did homage to her, the sun of suns; there the crystal, rose and jet were beautified by tenderness; her face was brighter than heaven's light; a dwelling-house was no fit abode for them, the sky itself was their (proper) palace.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 30 ('Story of Avtandil's Return to Arabia', Stanza 685; Wardrop Stanza 667): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Arabia, is joyfully welcomed by Shermadin and King Rostevan, and recounts Tariel's full story to Queen Tinatin, who praises his fidelity and urges him to fulfill his oath to return and aid his sworn brother.

ყმასა მეფე ასრე უჭვრეტს, ვითა შვილსა ტკბილი მამა.

stanzas.english_translation: That day they made a feast; drinking and eating they made abundant. The king gazes on the knight, as a tender father on a son. They were both beautified by a snowfall on fresh snow, a dew on the rose; generously they gave gifts, pearls like small coin.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 30 ('Story of Avtandil's Return to Arabia', Stanza 686; Wardrop Stanza 668): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Arabia, is joyfully welcomed by Shermadin and King Rostevan, and recounts Tariel's full story to Queen Tinatin, who praises his fidelity and urges him to fulfill his oath to return and aid his sworn brother.

stanzas.english_translation: The drinking was done, the drinkers separated each to his own home; they suffered not the magnates to go, they set the knight near before them. The king inquires, and he relates what trials he had undergone, and then what he had seen and heard concerning the stranger.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 30 ('Story of Avtandil's Return to Arabia', Stanza 687; Wardrop Stanza 669): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Arabia, is joyfully welcomed by Shermadin and King Rostevan, and recounts Tariel's full story to Queen Tinatin, who praises his fidelity and urges him to fulfill his oath to return and aid his sworn brother.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მას ვახსენებდე, ნუ გიკვირს, თქმა მჭირდეს მიწყივ ახისა:
მზე თუ ვთქვა მსგავსი მისი და ანუ მისისა სახისა,
ვინ უნახავ ქმნის გონება ყოველთა კაცთა მნახისა,
და ვარდი დამჭნარი ეკალთა შუა შორს-მყოფი, ახ ის ა!”
stanzas.english_translation: "When I speak of him, be not astonished if I ceaselessly lament, saying: 'Ah me!' To the sun alone can I liken him, or the face of him, the extinguisher of the mind of all who see him; a wilted rose among thorns, alas! he is far away!
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 30 ('Story of Avtandil's Return to Arabia', Stanza 688; Wardrop Stanza 670): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Arabia, is joyfully welcomed by Shermadin and King Rostevan, and recounts Tariel's full story to Queen Tinatin, who praises his fidelity and urges him to fulfill his oath to return and aid his sworn brother.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
რა ჭირი კაცსა სოფელმან მოუთმოს მოუთმინამან,
ქაცვი ლერწამმან, ზაფრანა იმსგავსოს ფერად მინამან,
ავანდილ, მისმან მხსენებმან, ღაწვი ცრემლითა მინამან.
და წვრილად უამბო ამბავი მან, მისმან მონასმინამან.
stanzas.english_translation: "When unendurable Fate makes a man suffer grief, the reed becomes like a thorn, the crystal turns to saffron colour." While Avt’handil was telling this his cheeks were bedewed with tears. He told in detail the story he had heard from (Tariel).
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 30 ('Story of Avtandil's Return to Arabia', Stanza 689; Wardrop Stanza 671): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Arabia, is joyfully welcomed by Shermadin and King Rostevan, and recounts Tariel's full story to Queen Tinatin, who praises his fidelity and urges him to fulfill his oath to return and aid his sworn brother.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ქვაბნი წაუხმან დევთათვის, სახლად აქვს დევთა სახლები,
საყვარელისა მისისა ქალი ჰყავს თანა ნახლები,
ვეფხისა ტყავი აცვია, ცუდად უჩნს სტავრა-ნახლები,

stanzas.english_translation: "Having captured the caves in battle, he has for his house the abode of the Devis. He has the damsel of his beloved as his attendant. He is clad in panther's skin; he despises brocade and cloth of gold. No more sees he the world; an ever-new fire consumes him."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 30 ('Story of Avtandil's Return to Arabia', Stanza 690; Wardrop Stanza 672): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Arabia, is joyfully welcomed by Shermadin and King Rostevan, and recounts Tariel's full story to Queen Tinatin, who praises his fidelity and urges him to fulfill his oath to return and aid his sworn brother.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
რა დაასრულა ამბავი, საქმე მისისა ჭირისა,
ნახვა მის მზისა ნათლისა, მის თვალად არ დუხჭირისა,
ეამა; უქეს ვარდისა ხელი, მძლედ დანამჭირისა;

stanzas.english_translation: When he had finished the story--the matter of his grief--the sight of the light of that sun, not ugly to look upon, gladdened him. They praised his rose-like hand which had been firmly held. "This prowess is sufficient for thee since thou art the undoer of grief."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 30 ('Story of Avtandil's Return to Arabia', Stanza 691; Wardrop Stanza 673): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Arabia, is joyfully welcomed by Shermadin and King Rostevan, and recounts Tariel's full story to Queen Tinatin, who praises his fidelity and urges him to fulfill his oath to return and aid his sworn brother.

გამხიარულდა თინათინ ამა ამბისა სმენითა;
მას დღე იხარებს სმითა და ჭამისა არ მოწყენითა.

stanzas.english_translation: "Woe is me if I wander where, alas! the simoom burns the roamer; my heart is the target of an arrow, a dart is shot to pierce it; the term of my life seems by this day to be shortened to one-third; I long for a refuge, but the time is past for seeking shelter against troubles.

stanzas.english_translation: "Him who yesterday was an aloe planted, watered and fully grown in Eden, him to-day Fate thrusts through with her lance, pierces with her knife. To-day my heart is caught in a net of unquenchable fire. Now know I the way of the world; it is a tale and nonsense."

stanzas.english_translation: The knight went and sat in his chamber; sometimes he weeps; sometimes he swoons, but in spirit he is near his beloved, he is not cut off from her. Like verdure in hoarfrost the hue of his face fades; see how soon lack of sun is apparent on the rose!

stanzas.english_translation: Accursed is the heart of man, greedy, insatiable; sometimes the heart desiring joys endures all griefs; blind is the heart, perverse in seeing, not at all able to measure itself; no king, nor even death itself, can master it.

stanzas.english_translation: Thus spake he, weeping, with flowing tears. Once more he addressed his heart: "Patience is like the fountainhead of wisdom. If we endure not what can we do? How can we adapt ourselves to anguish? If we desire happiness from God we must accept griefs also."
